claim: Current stable MCP spec revision is 2025-11-25; defines Hosts/Clients/Servers over JSON-RPC 2.0 with stateful connections and capability negotiation; servers offer resources/prompts/tools, clients offer sampling/roots/elicitation.
quote: The protocol uses JSON-RPC 2.0 messages... Resources: Context and data... Prompts: Templated messages and workflows... Tools: Functions for the AI model to execute

claim: The 2026-07-28 release candidate is the largest revision since launch: stateless protocol core, Extensions framework, Tasks, MCP Apps, OAuth hardening; RC locked May 21 2026, final spec to publish July 28 2026.
quote: The release candidate for MCP 2026-07-28 is the largest revision of the protocol since launch... a stateless core that scales on ordinary HTTP infrastructure

claim: MCP defines two standard transports — stdio (subprocess, newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, stderr for logs) and Streamable HTTP (single endpoint, POST+GET, optional SSE). Details Mcp-Session-Id, 202/400/404/405 status codes, resumability via Last-Event-ID.
quote: The protocol currently defines two standard transport mechanisms... stdio... Streamable HTTP. Clients SHOULD support stdio whenever possible.

claim: Lifecycle: initialize request (protocolVersion, capabilities, clientInfo) -> initialize response (capabilities, serverInfo, optional instructions) -> notifications/initialized. Version negotiation: client sends latest; server echoes if supported else returns another version; client disconnects on mismatch.
quote: The client MUST initiate this phase by sending an initialize request... After successful initialization, the client MUST send an initialized notification

claim: Tools primitive: tools/list (paginated) and tools/call; Tool has name, title, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, annotations, execution.taskSupport; results carry content[] plus optional structuredContent; isError flag distinguishes tool execution errors from protocol errors; notifications/tools/list_changed.
quote: Tools in MCP are designed to be model-controlled... To invoke a tool, clients send a tools/call request... Structured content is returned as a JSON object in the structuredContent field

claim: Resources primitive: resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list; URI-identified; resources/subscribe + notifications/resources/updated and notifications/resources/list_changed; resources capability has optional subscribe and listChanged; resource not found error -32002.
quote: Resources in MCP are designed to be application-driven... The capability supports two optional features: subscribe... listChanged

claim: Prompts primitive: prompts/list and prompts/get; Prompt has name, title, description, arguments; prompts/get returns messages[] with role + content; user-controlled (e.g. slash commands); notifications/prompts/list_changed.
quote: Prompts are designed to be user-controlled... Typically, prompts would be triggered through user-initiated commands... For example, as slash commands

claim: 2025-11-25 changes vs 2025-06-18: experimental Tasks; icons metadata (SEP-973); OIDC discovery; incremental scope consent via WWW-Authenticate; OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents; JSON Schema 2020-12 default dialect (SEP-1613); tool name guidance; SDK tiering system; input-validation errors as tool errors.
quote: Add experimental support for tasks to enable tracking durable requests with polling and deferred result retrieval (SEP-1686). Establish JSON Schema 2020-12 as the default dialect

claim: Base protocol JSON-RPC 2.0 shapes: requests (id MUST be string/integer, MUST NOT be null, MUST be unique per session), result responses, error responses (code/message/data), notifications (no id). _meta key-name rules; icons; JSON Schema 2020-12 default.
quote: Requests MUST include a string or integer ID. Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be null... Notifications MUST NOT include an ID.

claim: Specification and documentation repository for MCP; schema.ts is the source of truth.
quote: Specification and documentation for the Model Context Protocol

claim: Tasks primitive lets servers start expensive work without blocking the connection (no hanging connections/fake progress); CIMD replaces Dynamic Client Registration with DNS+HTTPS-anchored decentralized trust.
quote: No more hanging connections or fake progress spinners. Clients can give users real progress.

claim: JSON-RPC batching was added in 2025-03-26 and removed in 2025-06-18, simplifying implementation for clients and servers.
quote: The removal of JSON-RPC batching support, which was introduced in 2025-03-26, simplifies the protocol implementation

claim: MCP replaced the legacy two-endpoint HTTP+SSE transport with single-endpoint Streamable HTTP starting protocol version 2025-03-26; Streamable HTTP is the recommended remote transport.
quote: MCP replaced the HTTP+SSE transport mechanism with Streamable HTTP starting from protocol version 2025-03-26

claim: stdio is local-only, single-client and simplest but collapses under concurrent load; Streamable HTTP is the choice for remote/multi-client servers.
quote: STDIO is local-only and single-client and is the simplest MCP transport but collapses under concurrent load.

claim: 2026 roadmap targets a stateless protocol core scaling on ordinary HTTP infrastructure plus an Extensions framework for optional capabilities.
quote: the 2026 roadmap: a stateless core that scales on ordinary HTTP infrastructure, extensions
